note: Economy difficulty. These multipliers change the PLAYER's operating position only; NPC carriers, prices and the rest of the world run on the base economy at every level, so a harder level means a harder life for you, not a different universe. target_margin is the net margin the benchmark ship (the starter) should earn on the reference lane mix; tests/test_economy_levels.gd checks each level lands inside its band, and tools like it retune the multipliers when the economy changes. Multipliers were solved with tests/solve_levels.gd (bisect freight_pay_mult against target margin); rerun it whenever base rates, fuel, ship costs or the starter ship change. freight_pay_mult above 1 is the owner-operator premium (small, odd and urgent loads pay more per SCU than trunk freight); the consignee pays it, so money is conserved.

benchmark.note: Share of time the ship has paid cargo (0.60) and the share of return legs that also carry paid cargo (0.55). Both are measured on starter-class stand-in captains in the Hopewell scenario (tests/test_player_economy.gd): 57-65% paid time. The stand-ins see freight before the NPC fleets, as the human does (carrier flag first_look). The backhaul figure fits the probe to the full simulation at the normal level; it has moved as the world gained frontier export chains and more carriers (30% -> 74% -> 55%). A sloppier captain idles more and loses money.

difficulty_ids_match: Level ids match Worlds.DIFFICULTIES ids, so the difficulty chosen at New Game selects the economy level.
